title: Please Be Alert: Fraudsters Are Impersonating First United
summary: Customers are receiving fraudulent texts and phone calls about Zelle® transfers. The caller may know personal or account information and may even claim to be a First United Bank & Trust employee. Do not let that convince you the call is legitimate.
body_markdown:
Customers are receiving fraudulent texts and phone calls about Zelle® transfers. The caller may know personal or account information and may even claim to be a First United Bank & Trust employee. **Do not let that convince you the call is legitimate.**


Remember:


- First United **DOES NOT send text messages regarding Zelle fraud** .
- We will **never ask you to provide a security code** .
- Never share your username, security codes, or screenshots of your account with someone who contacts you unexpectedly.


If something doesn’t seem right, **hang up and contact First United directly at1-888-692-2654 .**


1. **How the scam works**
Customers may receive a text asking whether they recognize a Zelle transfer, followed by a phone call from someone claiming to represent First United.
2. **Why it can seem legitimate**
The fraudster may know personal or account information, use a local-looking phone number, or identify themselves as a First United employee.
3. **What they are trying to obtain**
Fraudsters may request online banking usernames, screenshots, account information, or security/verification codes so they can gain access to move money.
4. **What customers should do**


- Do not reply to the text.
- Do not click links.
- Do not provide security or verification codes.
- Do not send screenshots of online or mobile banking.
- Hang up if someone requests this information.
- Contact First United directly through a trusted number or established banking channel.
- If information has already been provided, contact the bank **immediately at1-888-692-2654** .


[Learn More About Protecting Your Account](http://mybank.com/security)
